ticket.title: miter clones reports shape-identical code as duplication: add a content dimension and a repeated-block mode
ticket.description: Ran across all 11 repos at the default 0.90 similarity / 15-line floor: 776 functions, 100 clones, 17 of them cross-crate. Spot-checking the two highest-scoring cross-crate pairs showed both are shape-identical and data-different, so neither is duplication: benchwork-mcp list_tools (score 1.000) builds benchwork_ JSON schemas while benchwork-core list_suite_tools builds miter_/storypole_/chalkline_ definitions with zero shared strings; and miter engine name/base_level/universal_kind_code versus ast_indexer fmt (0.95) are match-self arms over different enums. Meanwhile the duplication that actually exists is invisible: Command::new("git").args(..).current_dir(..).output() appears 66 times across 24 files in outfeed, miter and storypole, and only the two instances at or above 15 lines were reported. Fix: compare identifier and string-literal sets alongside the structural hash, and add a repeated-block mode that counts n-gram blocks shorter than the function floor so wrapper boilerplate becomes a number.
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06, commit d24af8a (miter). Clone detection now compares content as well as shape.

The report was unusable rather than merely noisy: 1387 pairs at 85 percent over this suite, and among them `dado`'s `main` paired with `outfeed`'s `parse_header`. That pairing is impossible - the two functions do unrelated work - and a reader who finds one such pair discounts everything else in the report, including the pairs that are real.

The cause is structural: a fingerprint recorded control-flow shape and nothing else, and a `match`-and-`format!` skeleton appears in a large fraction of all functions. A fingerprint now also carries the identifiers the body names, and a pair must clear both thresholds. Content similarity is Jaccard overlap of the two identifier sets, defaulting to 0.35 - deliberately low, because genuine copy-paste with renamed locals still shares the API calls and type names it talks to. The filter is aimed at bodies that share a silhouette and nothing else.

Measured, same inputs and thresholds otherwise:
  before  1387 pairs, including dado main vs outfeed parse_header
  after    104 pairs, and no parse_header pairing at all
The survivors are dominated by HTTP handlers that genuinely are boilerplate - same shape, same vocabulary, different endpoints. That is a defensible finding for a reviewer, which is the bar: would someone act on it.

`--min-content` exposes the threshold and `--min-content 0` restores shape-only behaviour, so the old report is reproducible for anyone comparing.

Tests: a new fixture proves shape alone still matches at 0.0 and the same pair is dropped at 0.9. The pre-existing structural fixture now documents that it disables the content dimension deliberately, rather than being quietly relaxed - it exists to prove shape matching works, and its two functions name different things by design.

clones.rs hit 261 lines and split into clones/mod.rs (extraction: shape and names, 184) and clones/detect.rs (detection: thresholds and evidence, 87).

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, 281 tests green, audit clean.
